argument:
Microsoft grew revenue and operating income 18%, reaching $90.0bn and $40.6bn respectively. That matched operating growth and approximately 45.11% derived operating margin provide a stronger bull foundation than headline EPS. Azure growth of 43% and cloud growth of 27% show that demand is converting into reported revenue rather than remaining a generic AI narrative.

OpenAI investment gains and discrete EPS benefits must be normalised. Cloud gross margin declined with infrastructure and mix, while debt and FCF remain unreconciled; distributions alone do not establish funding sufficiency. The clear uptrend supports continued interest, but RSI above 76 and an upper-band extension limit confidence in chasing. The investment case depends on sustained operating profitability after capacity costs.
key_points: Revenue and operating profit growth provide a clean operating anchor.
Azure and cloud growth show realised demand conversion.
Margin pressure, cash-flow gaps and extended price timing constrain conviction.
